answer: The SybilGuard protocol treats the vouch graph as a comet‑shaped flow: each honest node emits a random walk that drifts toward a harbor of trusted anchors, and only walks that survive the tide of cuts are accepted as valid identities. A verifier initiates k=20 walks of length ℓ=30; any new node must appear on at least t=5 distinct walks that intersect a known anchor, otherwise it is rejected. To forge one fake identity an attacker must lock 10 000 tokens for one tide (≈24 h) and pay a transaction fee of 0.5 % per walk, yielding a total cost of 5 000 tokens per Sybil.
